issue_context.title: Cost model for normal index scan is different from index scan for a index join
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement
The cost formula of a normal index scan (in `(*DataSource).getOriginalPhysicalIndexScan()`) contains `nRanges * seekFactor`, but the formula of an index scan for an index join (in `(*LogicalJoin).constructInnerIndexScanTask()`) doesn't contain this part.
comments: It will be hard to really fix this issue because we can't get `Ranges` in `constructInnerIndexScanTask` now, and we may need to estimate `nRanges` here.

> It will be hard to really fix this issue because we can't get `Ranges` in `constructInnerIndexScanTask` now, and we may need to estimate `nRanges` here.

Seems using `len(helper.chosenRanges)` is reasonable.

review_comments: We change `ranges` here. Besides calculating seek cost of probe-side, it also affects the calculation of other costs since changing of `ranges` causes changing of `rowCount`. I'm not sure that whether `helper.chosenRanges.Range()` is suitable for estimating row count since it comes from `(*indexJoinBuildHelper).buildTemplateRange`, which seems to fill empty datum in some ranges.
After talking with @qw4990, `ranges` here only affects calculating seek cost of probe-side, it doesn't affect calculating row count or other stats. Hence it's OK.

`ranges` won't affect `rowCount` here ~
And actually, `helper.chosenRanges.Range()` is the only range we can use to calculate seek cost. In most cases, `chosenRanges` is `[NULL, NULL]` and `len(chosenRanges)` is 1, which is equal to what we use now `len(FullRange)`. For queries like `select /*+ use_index(t1, ab) */ * from t1, t2 where t1.a in (1, 2, 3) and t1.b=t2.b`, it can be large than 1 and more accurate than `len(FullRange)`.
